subject: Clarify billing and sample invoice lines for streaming partial outputs
messages:
From: Elaine Kim <elaine.kim@nimbushealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nimbus Health Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: concrete invoice lines for streaming sessions and disconnects

Hi Grace / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the streaming output looks promising for our clinical note assistant. Procurement has visibility now and they asked for two things before we can progress: a one-page example of how streaming sessions would appear on our monthly invoice, and a short explanation of how you bill for partial generations when connections drop or a client retries.

Specifically:
- If a user starts a streaming session, receives partially generated tokens, then disconnects and later resumes, how will that show up on the bill?
- If the SDK retries automatically and generates duplicate tokens, what is Redwood's policy for duplicate billing or credits?
- Can you provide a sample invoice snippet with line items grouped by session or by model-call? Procurement wants to compare to our current per-call billing with their legacy vendor.

I attached a quick rate request spreadsheet (nimbus_rate_request.xlsx) with our expected monthly call volume and some sample sessions. If you can return a one-page PDF example we can share in our procurement review that would be great.

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Kim
Head of Integrations, Nimbus Health
elaine.kim@nimbushealth.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: concrete invoice lines for streaming sessions and disconnects

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear ask and for the spreadsheet. Looping in Marissa (accounts) and Ben (pricing) so we can give you both the product-side explanation and an invoice mock.

Short answers up-front:
1) Billing surface: by default our hosted API bills per-token generated with a separate line for streaming sessions if customers opt into session-level visibility. For procurement comparisons we can provide either per-call token lines or aggregated session rows.
2) Partial generations on disconnect: we bill for tokens that were emitted by the runtime (i.e., bytes/tokens delivered by the stream). If a client disconnects after partial output, those tokens are billed.
3) Retries: automated retry attempts that result in duplicate tokens are excluded from billing when they are retried by our SDK within the configured "session resume window" (default 30s). If a customer performs a deliberate replay beyond that window we treat it as a new generation unless you enable idempotency keys.

I'll let Marissa propose a sample invoice layout and Ben confirm discounts/credits language. Expect a one-page PDF and a short explainer in the next 4–6 hours.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Director | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Kim <elaine.kim@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: concrete invoice lines for streaming sessions and disconnects

Elaine — attached is the one-page PDF (sample-invoice-lines.pdf) and a short set of invoice patterns. I also pulled a quick example from our billing schema so you can see exact fields we would populate. Below is the human-readable version (we can tailor the fields if procurement needs different keys).

Sample invoice patterns (human-readable):
- Line Type: streaming_session
  - Description: Streaming session (model:gpt-large, start:2026-11-01T10:05:12Z, end:2026-11-01T10:05:46Z)
  - Quantity: 1 session
  - Usage Detail: 1,240 tokens generated (billed_tokens: 1,240)
  - Unit Price: $0.0009 per token
  - Line Total: $1.116

- Line Type: streaming_partial_segment
  - Description: Partial generation pre-disconnect (session_id: s-0a1b2c, segment: 1)
  - Usage Detail: 420 tokens emitted before disconnect
  - Unit Price: $0.0009 per token
  - Line Total: $0.378

- Line Type: retry_dedup_credit
  - Description: SDK automatic retry within resume window (session_id: s-0a1b2c, retry_id: r-99)
  - Usage Detail: 210 duplicated tokens suppressed from bill
  - Line Total: -$0.189 (credit)

Key policies (short):
- Emitted tokens are the billing unit. If the server emitted bytes/tokens to the client, we consider them billable.
- Resume window: default 30s. SDK automatic reconnects that replay the last N tokens within this window use idempotency/checkpointing to avoid double-billing. Those duplicates are zeroed out and appear as a credit line (retry_dedup_credit).
- Backfill / server-side replays: if our runtime backfills lost tokens after a transient internal error, we do not double-bill; those are reconciled as internal credits before invoice issuance.
- Prorated session fees: for customers who purchase session bundles or reserved throughput we can include a prorated session charge line; otherwise we default to per-token unit pricing.

Attached files: sample-invoice-lines.pdf (PDF, 18KB) — contains a rendered mock invoice and a condensed explanation for procurement.

If procurement wants the exact JSON keys for automated ingestion we can provide a sample payload (billing_line_id, start_ts, end_ts, model, billed_tokens, unit_price_usd, currency). Would you like that?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Billing Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Marissa / Grace — this is exactly what procurement asked for, thank you. A couple of quick follow-ups:
- Can you confirm the resume window is configurable per-customer and if so what the SLA is for applying custom window settings?
- For customers who want session-level aggregation instead of per-token lines, can you provide a sample monthly aggregation row (e.g., total sessions: 12,354; total billed tokens: 4,321,881; avg tokens/session: 350) and an example of how discounts would show (percentage vs effective unit price)?

If you can add a JSON sample payload for ingestion (billing_line_id, start_ts, end_ts, model, billed_tokens, unit_price_usd, credit_flag) that would help our data engineering team ingest Redwood lines into our ledger.

If possible, can we have the JSON and the customized resume-window SLA text by end of day tomorrow? Procurement is meeting Thu morning PST.

Thanks again — Elaine
